tagline: Architecture-aware Specs, Spec-derived grants and fenced Claude Code workers.
title: Concorde Framework

homepage.title: Specify the architecture. Fence your agents.
homepage.description: Concorde keeps your project's Specs at the center of AI-assisted development. Its Spec tooling validates the Specs, computes from them exactly what a task may read and write, serves them over a local MCP server and publishes them as this site. Your Claude Code session, the main agent, splits work into tasks and runs Concorde's Operations, whose headless Claude Code workers run inside the Spec-derived boundary and whose results keep host evidence apart from worker claims.

features.title: Context and permission, managed around the Spec.

items.title: Read complete Module specifications.
items.description: Module documents explain purpose, terminology, use, design and relationships for a reader who does not know the code. Implementation documents hold the precise requirements, scenarios and contracts, and tests declare the scenarios they verify.

items.title: Grants computed from the Specs.
items.description: The Spec Protocol defines six task types — understand, specify, implement, test, review-spec, review-code — and the access level each gives every boundary set. A grant lists every path a task may know by name, read or write; everything else is denied.

items.title: Workers fenced by their own settings.
items.description: Each worker is a headless claude -p process with generated deny rules (which also bind its Bash sandbox), a write-only hook, a sandbox without network, a cleared environment and its own configuration directory. The host audits every round against the grant. These guard against drift and mistakes, not a malicious actor.

items.title: Operations: host steps plus workers.
items.description: understand, specify, implement, test, spec_review and code_review run workers; validate and delivery are deterministic. The host runs configured checks itself, resumes a worker only to fix failing checks, and stops with an escalation on a Spec gap or a boundary it would have to cross.

items.title: Tasks are branches.
items.description: Each task is a branch with its own worktree, a record and a decision log. Tasks run in parallel only in separate worktrees; delivery commits the change with its evidence and the main agent merges it.

items.title: Spec tooling that stands alone.
items.description: concorde validate, concorde grant and the stdio MCP server concorde spec-mcp answer from the Specs of one worktree without calling a model, so any agent can ask what a task may touch.

workflow.title: One task from idea to merge.
workflow.description: The main agent agrees the direction with the developer, then works through a task; it decides ordinary questions itself and escalates only decisions with major impact.

steps.title: Discuss & open
steps.description: Agree the change with the developer and open a task: a branch and worktree for the Modules it touches.

steps.title: Understand & specify
steps.description: Run understand to assess and plan; run specify when the Spec must change first.

steps.title: Implement & test
steps.description: Run implement and test; the host audits every write and runs the configured checks itself.

steps.title: Validate, deliver, merge
steps.description: validate decides readiness, delivery commits the change with its evidence, and the main agent merges the branch.

quickstart.title: Install into a Git project.
quickstart.description: Use Python 3.11+ and a logged-in Claude Code on Linux with bubblewrap. The installer places the runtime, the concorde command, the Protocol copy and the main-session guidance; it never writes your Specs. Claude Code is the only supported client in this version.
quickstart.code:
git clone https://github.com/FTOD/concorde.git
cd concorde
python3 scripts/concorde.py build
python3 scripts/install-concorde.py /absolute/path/to/project

cd /absolute/path/to/project
.concorde/bin/concorde init --propose --name "My project"

reference.title: Commands and Operations
reference.description: Everything runs through the concorde command; Operations print one JSON result.

tables.title: Operations
tables.description: Run with concorde run <operation> --task <task> in the task's worktree.
rows: understand
An assessment of the Modules and, when asked, a plan; reads Specs and only the names of code.
specify
A change of the bound Modules' own Spec documents; structural validation afterwards.
implement
A code change within the bound Modules' realization; configured checks with resume rounds.
test
The host's check results interpreted by a read-only worker.
spec_review
Review findings and a verdict on the bound Modules' Specs.
code_review
Review findings and a verdict on the task's code changes.
validate
Readiness: structural validation and the configured checks of the changed Modules.
delivery
A commit of the task's change with its evidence bundle on the task branch.

tables.title: Commands
tables.description: In an installed project the command is .concorde/bin/concorde.
rows: concorde validate
Check every structural rule of the Specs.
concorde grant --modules <ids> --type <task type>
Print the grant of a task type for some Modules.
concorde spec-mcp
Run the local stdio MCP server rooted at the project.
concorde task open|list|show|close
Manage tasks: branch, worktree, record and decision log.
concorde run <operation> --task <task>
Run one Operation and print its result.
concorde init --propose|--apply
Propose and apply a project's first Spec.
concorde docsite --propose|--apply
Scaffold a documentation site for the project's Specs.
